chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

"The minimum that suffices you from supplication after the obligatory prayer is that you say: O God, I ask You from every good which Your knowledge encompasses, and I seek refuge in You from every evil which Your knowledge encompasses. O God, I ask You for Your well-being in all my affairs, and I seek refuge in You from the disgrace of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter."
ai.seo_question: What is the minimum recommended supplication to recite after obligatory prayers in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* via the chain of Zurarah, this hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) establishes a concise yet comprehensive post-prayer supplication that encapsulates the essence of divine mercy and protection. It reflects the Shia emphasis on integrating specific theological concepts—such as 'afiyah' (comprehensive well-being) and the duality of worldly disgrace versus Hereafter punishment—into daily ritual practice. This minimal yet potent dua serves as a spiritual anchor, ensuring the believer remains mindful of God’s all-encompassing knowledge after the physical act of prayer concludes.
